interactions.summary: Jiang stages a Yale thought experiment, then answers it himself: the problem is not the act alone but an ethos of self-indulgent inwardness, which he names as narcissism shared by homosexuality and incest.

speaker_notes.note: A brief UNKNOWN interjection appears to be conversational filler rather than a substantive new speaker turn.

claims.claim: Jiang says the real issue is an attitude of self-indulgence: be yourself, love yourself, do not worry about others, and do not assume responsibility for society.
Jiang claims homosexuality and incest both represent inward churning and extreme narcissism rather than outward social obligation.
When asked whether this means same-sex desire is not real love, Jiang answers that loving other men is really a form of loving oneself.

signature_moments.moment: Homosexuality is cast as narcissism because the beloved is treated as one's own reflected self.
signature_moments.source_phrase: what you're really doing is loving yourself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the sharpest and most combustible compression of Jiang's interpretation in this section.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: An inward-churning self-love that turns apparent eros into a mirror relation and severs obligation to others.

chronology_notes.note: This packet is the lecture's strongest recoding of the sexuality debate into a broader diagnosis of narcissistic social inwardness.

uncertainty_notes.note: The mirror/Narcissus analogy is explicit but highly charged; keep it dated to this lecture and do not normalize it into undated corpus language.
